direction: What is kept and whom we care for: inexpensive beads saved as memory, an artist’s ordinary kindness to a dog, and paired door leaves holding a remembered village. Small still life, cropped human scene and architectural space vary distance and density. New literary interpretations, not historical or documentary claims.

items.title: Pearls kept in a box
items.rationale: Pearldom ends with cheap scattered beads gathered into a box, intimacy kept as memory. Show that unglamorous act’s aftermath, neither a luxury jewellery advertisement nor an invented couple.

review.notes: Normal-size review: seven inexpensive cream beads with subdued unequal reflections rest in a physically coherent thin cardboard box. Broken thread and one visible hole make their former connection legible; contact shadows agree with light. Empty paper and irregular spacing preserve intimacy rather than a jewellery display. No real-person or historical object claim; watercolor edges and graphite corners remain soft.

items.alt: Seven off-white beads and a short broken thread lie in a small plain cardboard keepsake box.

items.title: Beside the painter
items.rationale: The poem’s resolution is the artist quietly comforting the dog and continuing to make art after contempt has passed. Depict care in this ordinary shared space, without presenting a real portrait or showing cruelty.

review.notes: Normal-size review: anonymous cropped painter’s forearm and relaxed hand contact the dog naturally; dog has two forelegs, two partly overlapping rear feet, one tail and supported resting torso. Board and tin are anchored, broad blue/ochre gouache planes and quiet open space carry kindness without sentimentality or invented identity. Two brushes appear rather than one but do not add clutter or change meaning. No depicted abuse, injury, real-person likeness or documentary claim.

items.alt: A cropped anonymous painter rests a hand on a calm brown dog beside an unfinished board and paint tin.

items.title: Two leaves of a door
items.rationale: The village held within the speaker culminates in an old paired wooden door and remembered connection across its two sides. Preserve that grounded architectural memory without inventing the poet’s actual village, a shrine or an ornate heritage monument.

review.notes: Paired geometric marks on upper door panels resemble invented cultural symbols. Keep only simple existing rectangular joinery and natural wood grain.

Normal-size source/v2 comparison: all unexplained wavy lines, dashes and triangular symbols are removed. Simple rectangular panel carving, paired leaves, hinge attachments, latch and perspective remain coherent. Door surfaces retain natural grain and lower wear, with gentle courtyard light and spacious limewashed wall. Emotional connection survives without invented heritage motifs or a claim to depict the poet’s actual village. Selected v2; v1 retained.

items.alt: Two old wooden door leaves stand partly open within a modest frame, revealing light across an earthen threshold.

text_led.rationale: Keep the poem’s witness to Manipur and violence against women in the author’s words; do not invent documentary victims or turn suffering into decorative imagery.
The five linked river haiku change viewpoint and weather through brief encounters; keep their pauses rather than picking one scene or making a collage.
The urgent appeal to unteach hate carries itself in direct address. Avoid an ambulance, blood bottle or slogan graphic that could distract from that demand.
